description: The reviewed protocol material establishes the Minter and validator framework but does not normalize every legal entity, collateral SPV, reserve holder, and service provider involved across Minters.
notes: Do not represent M holders as having a uniform direct claim against one issuer or one collateral pool.

description: The complete current map of canonical M contracts, wrapped M, cross-chain representations, and M0 Extensions is not normalized.
notes: Extensions and wrapped representations must not be collapsed into the base M identity.

description: Minter mint and burn mechanics are documented, but a universal holder right to redeem M directly into a specified collateral pool is not established.
notes: Keep redemption modeled as protocol and Minter dependent.

description: Per-Minter collateral schedules, validator reports, and reserve disclosures are not yet normalized into one comparable current reserve view.
notes: The reserve context row records the framework rather than a periodic consolidated attestation.

description: Official material establishes the USDf product and a 2025 launch period, but the reviewed sources do not fix one authoritative day-level launch boundary.
notes: Preserve launch_date as null until a durable dated primary source is normalized.

description: The complete legal issuer, collateral owner, custodian, hedging counterparty, and bankruptcy-treatment map is not normalized from one durable source set.
notes: Do not infer a direct holder claim or bankruptcy remoteness from collateral and transparency descriptions alone.

description: The reviewed Ethereum contract is recorded, but the complete set of native, bridged, and supported USDf deployments is not normalized.
notes: Add deployments only after canonicality and bridge control are established.

description: Transparency and assurance materials exist, but the latest assurance date, scope, publisher, collateral split, and recurring publication history are not normalized into one dated snapshot.
notes: The current reserve row points to the official index rather than asserting a current percentage allocation.

description: The relationship between the historical dForce USX product, current USX Finance presentation, governance, and operating organizations is not fully normalized.
notes: One continuous token identity is retained provisionally unless contract or migration evidence proves replacement.

description: Current documentation uses yield-bearing language for USX while also distinguishing sUSX; whether the base token itself accrues value across current deployments remains unresolved.
notes: The income profile records wrapper access and keeps the unresolved base-token semantics explicit.
